info.title: FreeTicket B2B API
info.description:
FreeTicket B2B REST API for integrations, the `ft` CLI and the FreeTicket MCP server. Authentication is by API key (`Authorization: Bearer <key>` header or `x-api-key`); the active workspace is selected with the `X-Workspace-Id` header.

Scopes: each key is either `read` (GET/HEAD only) or `write` (additionally creates, edits, deletes, cancels, refunds and checks in). Self-service keys are issued as `read`. A `read` key calling a mutating method gets a 403. The machine-readable declaration lives at `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` (RFC 9728).

Getting a key (self-serve, no sales contact): `ft login` runs the Device Authorization Grant (RFC 8628, `POST /auth/device/code` + `POST /auth/device/token`); the user approves the code at https://admin.appfreeticket.com/device and the CLI receives a key. New organizers can bootstrap headless with `POST /auth/signup` (verify-first, then `ft login`). With a key, `POST /api-keys` mints more (born `read` unless `write` is requested). There is no sandbox environment: test against a dedicated workspace with `read` keys.

## Versioning and deprecation

- **Path version.** The B2B API is versioned in the path (`/api/v1`). A breaking change ships under a new path (`/api/v2`); the previous version keeps running in parallel until its sunset date.
- **Contract version.** `info.version` is the semantic version of this document. MINOR = additive (new endpoints, new optional fields, new enum values, new error codes; clients must ignore unknown fields). PATCH = documentation or fixes that do not change shapes. The public API (`/api/public`) is pre-1.0 and not versioned in the path: there, a MINOR bump may include a breaking change and PATCH never does.
- **Deprecation signals.** A deprecated operation is marked `deprecated: true` in this document and its responses carry `Deprecation` (RFC 9745, e.g. `Deprecation: @1767225600`), `Sunset` (RFC 8594, an HTTP-date after which the operation may stop working) and `Link: <https://appfreeticket.com/desarrolladores>; rel="deprecation"`.
- **Timeline.** At least 6 months between the first `Deprecation` header and the `Sunset` date for `/api/v1`, and at least 90 days for `/api/public`. A path version is only retired after all its operations have sunset.
- **Current status.** No operation is deprecated today.

## Rate limits

- **429 always carries `Retry-After`** (seconds). Wait at least that long before retrying the same request. The JSON error envelope comes with `error.retryable: true`; most rate-limited responses use `error.code: "RATE_LIMITED"`, and some return a more specific code (for example `TOO_MANY_REQUESTS` or `SEAT_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`).
- **RateLimit headers are sent where listed below.** Those endpoints answer every response, success or error, with the IETF RateLimit headers (draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers): `RateLimit-Policy: "<policy>";q=<quota>;w=<window seconds>` and `RateLimit: "<policy>";r=<remaining>;t=<seconds until reset>`. Other endpoints may answer 429 without them.
- Counters are fixed windows kept per server instance: treat the numbers as pacing hints, not as a global account quota.

Endpoints that send RateLimit headers today: `POST /auth/signup` (per client IP), `POST /customer/auth/request` and `POST /customer/auth/verify` (per client IP), and the buyer-session endpoints `GET /customer/orders/{id}`, `POST /customer/orders/{id}/payment`, `/payment/card`, `/payment/pse`, `/release`, `POST /customer/purchase-sessions` and `POST /customer/purchase-sessions/{id}/release`.

get.summary: Merch store catalog of the key's brand
get.description: Requires an enterprise service API key (Legend headless landing, called server-side); the store is ALWAYS the one of the key's organization. Returns the store settings (brand, support, shipping fees by zone — Bogotá is DANE 11001 —, free-shipping threshold, delivery modes), the PUBLISHED products with their active variants and `stock` (units available right now, already net of open 15-minute reservations), the active pickup points (only when pickup is enabled) and the public key of the brand's own MercadoPago account for the Payment Brick. Prices are COP integers, VAT included; the buyer pays no service fee. Preview: with a valid `X-Merch-Preview` token (issued by the dashboard for this key's store, 1 hour) the response also includes DRAFT products (each product carries `status`), answers even while the store onboarding is pending, sets `preview: true` and `Cache-Control: private, no-store`; an invalid or expired token silently returns the public catalog. Preview never enables ordering: `POST /merch/orders` only sells PUBLISHED products. 403 `MERCH_STORE_LOCKED` when the brand's Legend plan is not active; 404 `STORE_NOT_READY` when the brand has no store, its onboarding is incomplete or it has no connected MercadoPago account (a valid preview token is exempt). `mpPublicKey` is the public key of the brand's own MercadoPago account.

post.summary: Publish an event
post.description:
Minimum role: `ADMIN`. Active workspace via the `X-Workspace-Id` header.

Publishes the event and its dates (cancelled dates stay cancelled unless the whole event was `CANCELLED`). Requires at least one future date (409 `CONFLICT`).

Seated (seats.io) events are validated first:
- 409 `SEATSIO_INVALID`: a seated date has no ticket type mapped to a chart category, or maps a category missing from the chart.
- 409 `SEAT_MAP_CATEGORIES_UNCOVERED`: a chart category with seats on sale has no ticket type on that date and is not fully blocked (booked). `error.details.zones[]` lists each one (`dateLabel`, `categoryKey`, `categoryLabel`, `seats`). Create its ticket type or block those seats, then retry.
- 503 `SEAT_MAP_UNVERIFIABLE` (retryable): seats.io could not be reached to verify the map.

Paid events (any ticket type with price > 0) require the workspace identity verification to be approved:
- 409 `IDENTITY_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED`: the event stays `DRAFT` and is queued; it publishes automatically within ~5 minutes of the verification being approved.

put.description:
Minimum role: `ADMIN`. Active workspace via the `X-Workspace-Id` header.

Replaces the artists linked to the event with `artistIds`, in that order (the lineup order). Artists not in the list are unlinked (send the full lineup, not a diff); `[]` clears it. Ids come from `GET /artists?q=` (workspace ids of registered artists). Newly linked artists get a notification email.

`inviteEmails` invites artists without an account: each email gets an invitation (only once per email and event) and is linked when it signs up. `inviteEmails` is additive: omitting it does not cancel existing invitations (use `DELETE /events/{id}/artist-invitations/{invitationId}`).

Ids that are not a registered artist (or the event's own workspace) are skipped and reported in `warnings[]` with code `ARTIST_IDS_IGNORED` (`ids`).

Limits: up to 50 `artistIds` and 20 `inviteEmails` per request; 20 lineup changes per hour per API key and event (429 `RATE_LIMITED` with `Retry-After`).

post.summary: Grant read-only access to an event's statistics
post.description:
Minimum role: `ADMIN`. Active workspace via the `X-Workspace-Id` header.

Gives the owner of `email` read-only access to this event's statistics and emails them the link. If no account exists for that email, a read-only (`VIEWER`) account is created with no access to the rest of the workspace, and a second email lets them set a password. The response does not say whether an account already existed (`newAccount` is deprecated and never sent). Idempotent per event and person: 201 when the access is new, 200 when it already existed (the notice email is sent again). 502 `EMAIL_NOT_SENT` when the email provider failed (the access WAS granted; retry to resend). Rate limited: 10 invitations per 10 minutes per API key (429 `RATE_LIMITED` with `Retry-After`).

post.summary: Add a ticket validator to an event
post.description:
Minimum role: `ADMIN`. Active workspace via the `X-Workspace-Id` header.

Assigns door staff to this event. If no account exists for `email`, a `STAFF` account is created in the workspace and an invitation email is sent so they can set a password (`invited: true`). If the person is already a validator of this workspace, they are reactivated and this event is added to their list (assignments are additive: existing events are never removed; a validator with no events assigned already validates every event of the workspace, so nothing is added and they keep `allEvents: true`). `userId` and `name` are only returned when the person is a member of the active workspace (otherwise only the `email` sent is echoed). 409 `VALIDATOR_OTHER_WORKSPACE` when that person cannot be assigned as a validator of this workspace (the message is intentionally generic). To remove a validator, change their access with `PUT /staff/{id}/access` or revoke it with `DELETE /staff/{id}`. Rate limited: 10 per 10 minutes per API key (429 `RATE_LIMITED` with `Retry-After`).

post.description: Marks the sale as CANCELLED, releases its inventory and frees the associated numbered seats. IMPORTANT: a sale with tickets already used at the door is NOT cancelled: it responds 409 SALE_ALREADY_CHECKED_IN, because returning that inventory would put it back on sale with the person already inside. IMPORTANT: a PENDING sale charged through Bold has a payment link that may still be live — the Bold API never marks its links as expired —, so cancelling it could leave the buyer charged without a ticket. Before cancelling, the actual payment status is re-read: if Bold reports it approved, it responds 409 SALE_PAID_AT_GATEWAY and the sale is NOT cancelled under any circumstances (that sale gets confirmed or refunded). If the payment is still open or its status cannot be read, it responds 409 OPEN_PAYMENT_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED: check the Bold dashboard and repeat the call with {"acknowledge_open_payment": true} to explicitly accept the risk. A sale charged with a Bold card terminal (counter sale) that still has a terminal charge in progress, or an approved charge not yet delivered, responds 409 TERMINAL_CHARGE_IN_PROGRESS and is not cancelled (the acknowledgement does not override it). Sales from other gateways and sales with no payment started are cancelled without that step.

put.summary: Replace a staff member's access in this workspace
put.description:
Minimum role: `ADMIN`. Active workspace via the `X-Workspace-Id` header.

DESTRUCTIVE (full replace): sets what the user can do in the active workspace and removes whatever is not in the body. `accessType`: `admin` (role `ADMIN`, everything; only a `SUPER_ADMIN` can grant it, otherwise 403 `ADMIN_REQUIRES_SUPER_ADMIN`), `validador` (role `STAFF`, ticket validation only; `validatorEventIds` limits which events, empty = all events of the workspace), `personalizado` (role `STAFF`, only the listed `sections`; including `validar` also enables validation, limited by `validatorEventIds`) or `lectura` (role `VIEWER`, read-only statistics of `viewerEventIds`). `expiresAt` (`YYYY-MM-DD`, end of that day in the workspace timezone; null = permanent). `expiresAt` in the past is rejected (422). Event ids must belong to the workspace (422 `INVALID_EVENTS`). Nobody can change their own access (409 `SELF_ACCESS`). Only a `SUPER_ADMIN` can change the access of a user whose global role is `SUPER_ADMIN`, `ADMIN` or `MINCULTURA`, or who is an `OWNER`/`ADMIN` of the organization that owns the workspace (403 `TARGET_ROLE_FORBIDDEN`). 409 `VALIDATOR_OTHER_WORKSPACE` when the access enables ticket validation and the user cannot be assigned as a validator of this workspace (nothing is written). patch.description:
Minimum role: `ADMIN`. Active workspace via the `X-Workspace-Id` header.

Moves an ALREADY SOLD ticket to another `ticketTypeId` and/or to the `eventDateId` date (at least one of the two is required). Intended for a postponement: moving buyers from the old date to the new one without refunding and reselling.

It does NOT charge or refund the price difference if the new type costs something else: the ticket's `unitPrice`/`subtotal` keep the sale's ORIGINAL price. If money needs adjusting, use `POST /sales/{id}/refund` separately.

It does NOT reissue the QR: `ticketCode` is always preserved (it is what the buyer already has printed, in Wallet and in their email).

It does NOT notify the buyer. This endpoint only moves data; to resend the updated ticket use `POST /tickets/{ticketCode}/resend`, and for a bulk postponement notice, use the communications module.

A ticket that is already checked in, or that belongs to a sale that is not CONFIRMED, responds 409 and is not reassigned. A ticket refunded by item (or whose seat was blocked after a refund) responds 409 `TICKET_REFUNDED`.

NUMBERED SEATING (seats.io): if the target date has numbered seating, `seatLabel` is REQUIRED (409 `SEAT_REQUIRED` if missing) — the server never picks a seat on its own. The seat is validated and booked in seats.io before moving the ticket; if it is no longer available, it responds 409 `SEAT_UNAVAILABLE` without changing anything. If the ticket held a numbered seat on the source date, that seat is released after the move is confirmed.

Only event dates on sale: published event and current event date (otherwise 404). Limits: 10 creations per minute per buyer, 30 per minute per IP when called without an API key, and a global ceiling per event date (429 `RATE_LIMITED`). post.description:
Minimum role: `ADMIN`. Active workspace via the `X-Workspace-Id` header.

Send exactly one of:
- `publishAt`: the DRAFT publishes itself at that instant (checked every ~5 minutes). Must be in the future and before at least one of the event's dates. The response's `publishAt` echoes it.
- `saleStartsAt`: publishes the DRAFT now and opens sales at that instant, setting `saleStartsAt` on every ticket type of the upcoming dates in the same transaction. Must be in the future and before the first upcoming date.

- 409 `EVENT_NOT_DRAFT`: only drafts can be scheduled (also when it got published concurrently).

- Seated (seats.io) events: 409 `SEATSIO_INVALID`, 409 `SEAT_MAP_CATEGORIES_UNCOVERED` (`error.details.zones[]`), 503 `SEAT_MAP_UNVERIFIABLE` (retryable) — same as `POST /events/{id}/publish`.
- 409 `IDENTITY_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED` (`saleStartsAt` on a paid event of an unverified workspace). Unlike `POST /events/{id}/publish`, the event is NOT queued: retry after the verification is approved.

post.summary: Create a merch order and reserve its stock
post.description: Requires an enterprise service API key AND a valid `X-Customer-Session` (401 without it); the buyer email is the session's (it is NOT sent in the body) and the order is always linked to that customer. The order belongs to the key's organization store (variant ids from another store respond 409 `VARIANT_UNAVAILABLE`). Creates a PENDING order and reserves the stock for 15 minutes, all-or-nothing: if any variant lacks units nothing is reserved (409 `OUT_OF_STOCK` with `details: [{ variantId, requested, available }]`). Prices, shipping and totals are computed server-side from the catalog (`total = subtotal - discountAmount + shippingFee`; shipping is 0 for pickup or above the free-shipping threshold). `maxPerOrder` is per product, adding all its variants (422 `MAX_PER_ORDER`). A product may also cap the units per person across ALL their orders that are not cancelled or refunded, matching by email or customer, and by buyer document or phone only on orders that are no longer PENDING; a cancelled order whose charge can still appear also counts (422 `MAX_PER_CUSTOMER` with `details: { productIds }`). On those products a customer can use at most 2 distinct documents in the store (422 `TOO_MANY_DOCUMENTS`). The document must be digits for CC, TI and NIT; separators and leading zeros are ignored when comparing; a delivery mode that is disabled, or an inactive pickup point, responds 422 `DELIVERY_UNAVAILABLE`. DANE codes are validated by shape (department 2 digits, city 5 digits starting with the department). Accepts `Idempotency-Key` (unique per store): retrying with the same key returns the order created on the first attempt (201 with `Idempotent-Replay: true`) without reserving stock again; the replay is only returned to the same customer as the original order (otherwise 422 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`). A customer with a live PENDING order in the store who places another one REPLACES it (the previous order is cancelled and its stock returned in the same transaction), unless that order already has a payment attempt in flight (409 `ACTIVE_ORDER_EXISTS`). A live PENDING order of ANOTHER customer with the same phone (normalized to E.164, any country code) also responds 409 `ACTIVE_ORDER_EXISTS` (the existing order is never revealed). Optional `X-Buyer-Ip` (the buyer's IPv4/IPv6, sent by the landing server-to-server; invalid values are ignored): at most 10 orders per 10 minutes per store and IP (429 `RATE_LIMITED`). Rate limited: 5 orders/min per customer (429 `RATE_LIMITED` with `Retry-After`). post.description: Requires an enterprise service API key AND a valid `X-Customer-Session` (401 without it). Only orders of the key's organization store that belong to the session's customer are reachable (an unknown code, a code from another brand and a code of another customer all respond the same 404 `ORDER_NOT_FOUND`). Receives the token the Payment Brick produced on the landing's domain and charges it through the MercadoPago Payments API with the brand's own MercadoPago account (FreeTicket's fee is retained per order), using the order total from the database (never one sent by the client); the optional `issuerId` the Brick returns is forwarded as is; the reservation is extended (capped at 45 minutes after creation) before the charge. Card only. `status` is `approved`, `pending` (normal: bank authentication or processing, also for an unrecognized MercadoPago status; confirmed later by webhook — poll `/merch/orders/lookup`) or `rejected` (business decline, reason in `message`; the order stays pending until its reservation expires, so the buyer can retry with another card) — all three return 200. post.summary: Refund a sale (moving the funds depends on the payment gateway)
post.description: Marks the sale as REFUNDED and releases the associated numbered seats. IMPORTANT: whether the money goes back to the buyer depends on the payment gateway and the payment method used. Sales charged through MercadoPago are fully refunded against the MercadoPago API (stable idempotency key per sale, so retries never refund twice) and marked only once MercadoPago confirms. A 503 GATEWAY_REFUND_PENDING means MercadoPago did not answer clearly: the sale stays CONFIRMED and repeating the same call is safe. Sales charged through Wompi by CARD are voided against the payment gateway before being marked. In every other case this endpoint does NOT trigger the actual refund: the money is NOT returned automatically and a 200 only confirms the accounting status change. Those refunds must be handled separately in the payment gateway's dashboard. PARTIAL REFUND BY TICKET: send `items` with the ids of the sale items to refund (the `id` field of GET /sales/{id}/tickets). Each item refunds its prorated share of the sale total (by item subtotal; shares always add up to the exact total). The refunded tickets are invalidated at the door and their quota returns to stock; when no live item remains the sale becomes REFUNDED. Only MercadoPago (or uncharged / cash sales) support partial refunds: Wompi and Bold answer 409 GATEWAY_REFUND_NOT_SUPPORTED. Items already checked in answer 409 ITEM_ALREADY_CHECKED_IN — also for a FULL refund (no `items`, or all of them): a sale with any checked-in ticket is never refunded whole; refund the unused tickets by item; items from another sale answer 422 ITEM_NOT_IN_SALE; a refund already in flight over the same items answers 409 REFUND_IN_PROGRESS (retry exactly the same items). `block_seats: true` (also valid for a full refund) keeps the refunded numbered seats OUT of sale: seats.io moves them from booked straight to a blocked status, never through free. The `refund` object in the response reports the refunded amount and what happened to the seats. Wompi payment methods without API refunds (PSE, Nequi, Bancolombia transfer) respond 409: return the money in the Wompi dashboard and repeat the call with {"acknowledge_manual": true} to reflect the accounting status. A 502 means the gateway rejected the void and the sale remains CONFIRMED.

post.description: Requires the `X-Customer-Session` header. The enterprise service API key is OPTIONAL (with a key, results are additionally scoped to the workspace pinned to it). post.description: Requires the `X-Customer-Session` header. The enterprise service API key is OPTIONAL (with a key, results are additionally scoped to the workspace pinned to it). Abandons the PENDING sale and returns its inventory (and its seats) to stock, so the buyer can start over without waiting for the reservation to expire. It is the counterpart of `pending_sale_in_progress`: when `POST /customer/orders` rejects with that `reason`, the landing page can offer *continue paying* (`/payment`, idempotent) or *start over* (this route). The enterprise service API key is OPTIONAL (with a key, results are additionally scoped to the workspace pinned to it). `{id}` accepts the `reference` (FT-…) or the sale id. If the sale is still PENDING and its payment goes through Bold, the authoritative payment status is re-read from Bold; between re-reads it responds with the internal status, which the webhook keeps up to date. `status` is `approved`, `pending` or `rejected`; `pending` is a NORMAL state (asynchronous payment methods take time) and the landing page must retry. `tickets` —with each ticket's `ticketCode`— is only present when `status` is `approved`. The route MAY rate-limit polling and respond 429: honor `Retry-After` and apply backoff. Polling every ~2 s fits comfortably, but do not treat any threshold as a guarantee.

maxPerCustomer.description: Maximum units per person across all their orders that are not cancelled or refunded, including cancelled orders whose charge can still appear. Matches by email or customer on any of those orders, and by buyer document or phone only on orders that are no longer PENDING. Document and phone are not verified, so the limit is soft. Omitted or null: no limit.

membersOnly.description: Only a buyer with an active membership in the organization can order it. Default false.

options.description: Up to 3 options (Talla, Color…). The variants must be EXACTLY the combinations of their values, each once (at most 100). No options = one variant with empty `attributes`.

values.description: Option values in display order, e.g. `["S", "M", "L"]`.

attributes.description: One value per option, keyed by option name: `{ "Talla": "M" }`.

sku.description: Unique in the whole store (case-insensitive). Letters, digits, `.`, `-`, `_`.

compareAtPrice.description: Strikethrough price; must be greater than `price`.

imageUrls.description: Ordered photos (the first is the cover). Each must be a `publicUrl` returned by `POST /merch/products/images/upload-url` for this organization. External URLs are rejected (they are never fetched).

Full ordered list (replaces the current one; the first is the cover). Each URL must be a `publicUrl` from `POST /merch/products/images/upload-url` for this organization, or one the product already has. Photos that leave the list are deleted from storage.

uploadUrl.description: Signed storage URL. `PUT` the raw file bytes to it with the same `Content-Type` as `mimeType`, no auth header. Single use.

publicUrl.description: Final public URL of the photo once uploaded. Pass it in `imageUrls`.

paymentStatus.description: Status of the latest payment event. Usually the payment gateway's RAW status in its own vocabulary. Values prefixed with `FT_` come from FreeTicket, not the gateway: currently `FT_SALE_APPROVED_POST_CONFIRM`, which marks that the gateway re-notified an already-confirmed charge — this is how Bold reports its refunds. A CONFIRMED sale with this status may have money refunded that is not yet recorded.

ticketCode.description: New ticket code (the previous QR is void).

ticketCodesRotated.description: true when the email changed: the previous QR codes are void (transferred tickets keep theirs).

seats.description: seats.io labels. Only for seated events.

holdToken.description: Hold token of the seats.io map session. Required if seats are sent.

nitDigit.description: Check digit. Required if idType is NIT.

returnUrl.description: Absolute URL of the landing page the buyer returns to. Validated against the enterprise domain allowlist and the workspace that owns the event; if it fails validation it is ignored and the purchase proceeds as usual.

RateLimitPolicy.description: Quota policies applied to this request (draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers), one list member per limiter: `"<policy>";q=<quota>;w=<window seconds>`. Example: `"public-orders";q=8;w=300`.

RateLimit.description: Remaining quota per policy (draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers): `"<policy>";r=<remaining>;t=<seconds until the window resets>`. Example: `"public-orders";r=7;t=280`.

RetryAfter.description: Seconds to wait before retrying (RFC 9110 §10.2.3). Always sent with a 429.

apiKey.name: Authorization
apiKey.description: API key prefixed with `Bearer `. Alternative: the `x-api-key` header with the raw key. Available scopes: `read` and `write` (see `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`).
